page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. Below them, one Latin paragraph running full width, then ten lines of Syriac set as a quotation, and a catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: rem, & quidem acerrimum; affirmant quippe, illum hac de re multa disseruisse, ac disputasse cum Cyni discipulis, quod notatur etiam in praefatione professionis fidei ejusdem, quae illius dissertationibus adversus Nestorianos, & Monophysitas hisce verbis praefixa legitur,

page.notes: The ten Syriac lines (Estrangelo-style script, set as a quotation) could not be read letter by letter at this scan resolution, so each is marked illegible with an estimated letter count; the lengths are approximate. The catchword "Cant" at the lower right is doubtful. The Latin is transcribed as printed, with the printed "qv" spellings normalised to "qu" as the u/v rule requires (qvippe, qvod, qvae). The first line begins mid-word with "rem", a fragment continued from the previous page.
